chunks: And from him, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud Al-Raqqi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Allah has not created any creation greater in number than the angels. Every evening, seventy thousand angels descend from the heavens. They perform Tawaf around the Holy Ka'bah for the night. When dawn breaks, they depart to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they ascend to the heavens before the sun rises. Then seventy thousand angels of the day descend. They perform Tawaf around the Holy Ka'bah for the day. When the sun sets, they depart to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say peace to him. Then they ascend to the heavens before the sun sets.
ai.seo_question: How do angels visit the graves of the Imams according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the cosmological significance of the Ahl al-Bayt by depicting a continuous celestial circuit where seventy thousand angels transition from the Ka'bah to the shrines of the Prophet, Ali, and Husayn. The specific sequence—prioritizing the Prophet, then Ali, then Husayn—mirrors the hierarchical spiritual authority (Wilayah) cherished in Shia tradition, while the twice-daily rhythm emphasizes the perpetual presence of divine witnesses honoring the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Dāwūd Al-Raqqi, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Allāh has not created any creation greater in number than the angels. Every evening, seventy thousand angels descend from the heavens. They perform Ťawāf around Bayt Al-Ḥarām (Ka’bah) until dawn, after which they proceed to the grave of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) and say Salām to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) to say Salām to him, after which they go to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) and say Salām to him; and then they ascend back to the heavens before sunrise. Then seventy thousand angels from among the angels of the day descend from the heavens. They (too) perform Ťawāf around Bayt Al-Ḥarām (Ka’bah) until sunset, after which they proceed to the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and say Salām to him. Then they go to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) to say Salām to him, after which they go to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) and say Salām to him; and then they ascend back to the heavens before nightfall.
